scores.claim_text: 2,474 Company-operated stores + ~1,000 franchise, ~29.6M sq ft, almost all leased.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts on GPS 8-Ks (2024-2026) — looking for material store-closure / lease-rejection 8-Ks.
scores.M_value: 44 hits, all routine quarterly earnings-press-release 8-Ks; no material store-closure or lease-rejection 8-K headlines. Internal disclosure consistent across periodic filings.
scores.interpretation: Store-count trajectory disclosure is concrete and the 10-K is the authoritative source. Lease-portfolio exposure (29.6M sq ft, almost all leased) is structural but is being managed; no 8-K signals of mass closure activity. Heuristic 11 (store-count trajectory) PASS in narrow sense; Heuristic 12 (long-tail lease portfolio) is a structural risk to monitor in MD&A footnotes but not a contradiction.

scores.claim_text: ~200 vendors in ~30 countries; top two vendors 9% and 8% of fiscal 2025 purchases; ~27% Vietnam, ~21% Indonesia.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts on Hanesbrands (HBI, CIK 0001359841) for 'Gap Inc' and 'Old Navy' mentions 2022-2026 — counterparty supplier corroboration test.
scores.M_value: HBI 10-Ks/10-Qs: 9 hits for 'Gap Inc' (primarily DEF 14A director-bio mentions, plus one 8-K); 0 hits for 'Old Navy'. Heuristic 7 absence-test: Gap is NOT named as a top wholesale-supplier customer of HBI.
scores.interpretation: Absence is consistent with the 10-K disclosure: Gap is a private-label-heavy retailer with diffuse vendor base (top vendor only 9%). It does not source meaningfully from large branded apparel suppliers like Hanesbrands. No HARD CONTRADICTION — Heuristic 7 threshold is not triggered because Gap does NOT claim large-supplier exposure. Vendor concentration (top 2 = 17%) and country concentration (Vietnam+Indonesia = 48%) are real exposures but consistent with private-label apparel norms.

scores.claim_text: Cash+ST inv $3.0B, debt $1.5B, no ABL borrowings, current ratio 1.75:1, FCF $823M; no going-concern.
scores.M_check: Two queries: (a) Simon Property Group (SPG, CIK 0001063761) for Gap mentions — landlord top-tenant disclosure; (b) Macerich (MAC, CIK 0000912242) similarly; (c) GPS own filings for 'going concern' since 2018 (negative control).
scores.M_value: SPG: 7 hits (earnings 8-K tenant supplements 2022-2023). MAC: 5 hits (10-K disclosures in every fiscal year 2022-2026). GPS 'going concern' search: 7 hits — ALL exhibits to ABL credit agreements containing standard going-concern covenant language (boilerplate negative covenants), NOT a going-concern qualifier on Gap itself. Heuristic 10 (delisting/going-concern marker) NEGATIVE.
scores.interpretation: Strong liquidity claim is consistent with external evidence. Major mall REITs continue to disclose Gap as a notable tenant through their most recent 10-Ks (MAC 2026-02-20), confirming Gap's operational continuity and ongoing rent-paying status. No going-concern qualifier has ever been issued in the search window. Heuristic 10 distress markers absent. This is a healthy-balance-sheet retail name, not a distress candidate.

scores.claim_text: Fiscal 2025 net sales +2% to $15.4B; store+franchise sales +1%, online sales +4%; gross margin 40.8% (vs 41.3%) — 50 bp compression.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts on GPS filings 2024-2026 for 'Athleta' and 'Banana Republic' (growth-narrative brands).
scores.M_value: Athleta: 28 hits; Banana Republic: 26 hits across the period. Both brands continue to be prominently disclosed in earnings 8-Ks and periodic filings. However, segment-level financial breakdown shows 'one reportable segment' aggregation, so brand-level comp trends are not externally testable from the M-side.
scores.interpretation: Heuristic 9 (comp-sales vs marketing tier): the headline narrative emphasizes 'transformation momentum,' but the financial-statement disclosure shows only +1% store/franchise comp and a 50bp gross-margin compression (with merchandise inventory +7% YoY — Heuristic 12 inventory-turn watch). This is a slow-bleed pattern consistent with the cohort calibration note: real top-line growth is modest, margin is going the wrong way, and inventory is building. Operating income flat at $1.1B and net income DOWN ($816M vs $844M) despite revenue growth. MODERATE severity: the disclosed numbers are internally consistent but the gap between transformation narrative and operating-margin trajectory is the watch-item. Tariff exposure (Vietnam 27%, Indonesia 21%) and IEEPA-tariff uncertainty (Feb 2026 Supreme Court ruling) further pressure go-forward margins.

scores.claim_text: Loyalty program rebranded as 'Encore' in Q1 fiscal 2026; private-label and co-branded credit cards via a third-party financing company.
scores.M_check: (a) edgar_fts on GPS for 'Encore' (internal); (b) Capital One for 'Gap Inc'; (c) Synchrony Financial (CIK 0001601712) for 'Gap Inc' (true card-issuer counterparty test).
scores.M_value: Encore in GPS filings: 1 hit (this 10-K itself — appropriately recent, as the program launched in Q1 fiscal 2026). Capital One 'Gap Inc' hits: 5, all DEF 14As (director-bio mentions, not card-program). Synchrony Financial 'Gap Inc' hits: 27 — strong indication that Synchrony is the third-party card issuer, with regular disclosure across their periodic filings.
scores.interpretation: Loyalty rebranding is too new to test operationally (only one filing reference; will need 12-24 months of post-launch disclosure to assess engagement KPIs). Counterparty corroboration on the card-program side is strong: Synchrony Financial discloses the Gap relationship 27 times. Heuristic 7 PASS — material counterparty exposure is bilaterally disclosed.

scores.claim_text: China franchise transition to Baozun closed January 2023; Taiwan transition announced Nov 2022 was abandoned Aug 27, 2025.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts on (a) GPS for 'Baozun' and (b) all filers for 'Baozun' (external corroboration via Baozun's own SEC filings — Baozun is a US-listed ADR, CIK 0001601805).
scores.M_value: GPS internal Baozun mentions: 19 hits across the 2022-2026 window — consistent disclosure of the original announcement, China closing, and Taiwan abandonment. All-filers: 128 hits (includes Baozun's own filings).
scores.interpretation: Heuristic 3 (planned vs operational) explicit stage-ladder test: announced (Nov 2022) -> executed for China (Jan 2023) -> NOT executed for Taiwan (Aug 2025 abandoned). Gap properly disclosed both the executed and the abandoned legs of the plan. Honest planned-vs-operational disclosure. PASS — no narrative overhang.

scores.claim_text: Supply-chain finance program: $390M outstanding (Jan 31, 2026) vs $387M prior year; $2.604B added / $2.601B settled in fiscal 2025.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts on GPS for 'supply chain finance' since 2022.
scores.M_value: 12 hits, present in every 10-Q and 10-K since 2023 (effective date of ASU 2022-04). Disclosure stable: ~$387-390M outstanding for two consecutive years.
scores.interpretation: SCF program is consistently and properly disclosed (post-ASU 2022-04). Balance is flat YoY ($387M -> $390M), invoices added/settled nearly equal ($2.604B / $2.601B). No evidence of extended payment terms stress or supplier-liquidity weaponization. Soft watch-item only; structurally fine.
